about: A blind structure for a target length (#115; decision 0200). As many levels of the chosen minutes as fit the target length with their breaks (a break after every so many levels, never after the last; at least one level; at most sixty stages). Big blinds come off the chip ladder 100, 120, 150, 200, 250, 300, 400, 500, 600, 800, then 1,000, 1,200 and so on; they climb the ladder evenly from the first level's big blind to a twentieth of the chips in play (starting stack times expected entries), each rounded to the nearest rung and always above the level before. The small blind is half the big blind; the ante, when asked for, is the big blind. Levels are written 'small blind/big blind ante A for M' and breaks 'break M', in minutes. The floor may change any level after.

cases.description: Eight hours of 20-minute levels for 60 entries of 30,000, a ten-minute break every four levels, a big-blind ante.
A two-hour turbo of 10-minute levels for 20 entries of 10,000: no breaks, no ante.
Exactly at the target length: four 30-minute levels and one five-minute break make 125 minutes. A first big blind of 180 rounds to 200.
A target shorter than one level still gets one level.
Too few chips to climb to: each level takes the next rung up, so the blinds still rise.
